主要内容: Tesla reported a larger-than-expected loss in its Q2 2019 earnings, with an adjusted loss of $1.12 per share, compared to the $0.40 expected by analysts. Revenue also fell short, at $6.35 billion versus the $6.41 billion forecast. This compares to an adjusted loss of $3.06 per share on $4 billion in revenue during the same period last year. Despite the shortfall, Tesla reaffirmed its full-year delivery guidance, aiming to sell 360,000 to 400,000 vehicles, mostly Model 3s. The company delivered around 158,200 cars in the first half of 2019 and needs to deliver over 200,000 in the second half to meet the low-end of its guidance. Tesla aims to increase production to 10,000 Model 3s weekly by the end of 2019. The company also plans to improve production at its existing factories, including its battery plant outside Reno, Nevada, and a car assembly in Fremont, California. Tesla is targeting the start of Model 3 production in China by the end of the year to benefit from lower costs and regulatory credits. The company reported a record in vehicle production and deliveries, selling 95,200 vehicles during the second quarter and producing 87,048 cars. However, the average sales price of its vehicles declined due to the rollout of the Model 3 Standard Range Plus and the sale of older Model S and Model X vehicles without upgraded powertrains. Tesla's average sale price for Model 3s in North America remained at $50,000. While sales of its energy storage products increased, solar energy product sales declined. Tesla reported a larger-than-expected loss in Q2 2019, leading to a decline in its stock price. The company generated $368.2 million in revenue from energy generation and storage products, a 2% decline compared to the same period last year. Tesla's Powerwalls are now installed at over 50,000 sites, supporting the adoption of renewable energy at home. The company revised its capital expenditures guidance down to $1.5 billion to $2 billion, previously expecting $2 billion to $2.5 billion. Tesla's liquidity improved following a $3 billion capital infusion in May, with a cash position of $5.0 billion. Despite a rise in stock price before the earnings update, Tesla shares declined 22% year-to-date. The company still expects to return to profitability in Q3 2019.
